correctness.rationale: The binary form of all three original quasinecklace conditions is equivalent to an initial longest zero-run, a final one, and bounded internal zero-gaps. It gives a unique coefficient count. Each cyclic necklace class contributes exactly its number of longest zero-runs in the primitive period, giving the upper bound z. Exact coefficient asymptotics and standard Burnside counts show the ratio tends to z for fixed positive z. Direct exhaustive checks to length 15 and explicit orbit checks through length 14 independently test all nontrivial steps; finite tests do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: This settles the precise composition-resolved candidate overhead in a natural auxiliary class introduced for colex necklace generation, proving the optimal per-content factor z for all positive contents and demonstrating unbounded overhead across exact contents. The result explains why a weight-at-most charging guarantee does not transfer verbatim to equal-weight slices. Both a full exact count and a rotation-level structural description are obtained; existing alternative fixed-density CAT algorithms are recognized rather than contradicted.
